name: Starter: Tagalog
about: Tagalog sentence order and verb focus in real, everyday sentences.

words.ako: I (ko: my, by me; akin: mine)
words.ng: of; marks an object or doer that isn't the topic
words.ikaw: you (ikaw, ka; mo: your, by you)
words.ang: marks the topic, often before a definite noun
words.sa: in, at, to; after sasama, sa amin means with us
words.kung: if; whether; before a question word, an indirect question (kung saan: where)
words.kami: we, not including you (amin: us, our)
words.nang: marks how or by how much (nang walang asukal; nang sampung minuto)
words.kita: I … you (tatawagan kita: I'll call you)

pahingi.about: To ask someone for something: Pahingi ng tubig.

kita-tayo.about: A casual, shortened Magkita tayo (let's meet): Kita tayo bukas!

pasensiya-na.about: An everyday way to say excuse me or sorry, often with po.

concept.line: Short pronouns and little words like ba, po and na go together just after the clause's first word or phrase, in their own order: Hindi ko alam; Nagsasalita ka ba ng Ingles?; Puwede mo bang isara…?
Tagalog usually puts the description or the action first and its topic after, often with no word for is, am or are: Guro ako (I'm a teacher); Masyadong maliit ang sapatos (the shoes are too small).
ang marks the sentence's topic, often a noun English would give the (ang pinto, ang tren), and si does the same before a person's name.
A pronoun changes with its role: ako is the topic, ko is my or by me, and sa akin is to or for me; ikaw or ka, mo, and sa iyo work the same way: Hindi ko alam; Ano ang pangalan mo?
ng marks an object or doer that isn't the topic, and whose (Umiinom ako ng kape; ang kotse ng tatay ko); before a person's name, ni marks a doer or whose: Hinihintay tayo ni Lola; ang kotse ni Lola.

words.means: pumupunta = go habitually; pupunta = will go

concept.line: A verb with -um- or mag- makes the one doing it what the sentence is about (ako, kami), and the thing done takes ng: Kumain kami ng pizza; Umiinom ako ng kape.
